landmarks.name: Palace of Versailles
landmarks.description: The dazzling royal palace where French kings held court, surrounded by spectacular gardens and gilded halls.

figures.name: Louis XIV
figures.title: The Sun King, King of France (1643–1715)
figures.previewQuote: I am the state, and Versailles is my masterpiece.

figures.name: Marie Antoinette
figures.title: Queen of France (1755–1793)
figures.previewQuote: They said I only cared for luxury. They never knew my heart.

figures.name: André Le Nôtre
figures.title: Royal Gardener and Landscape Architect (1613–1700)
figures.previewQuote: A garden should take your breath away before you take your first step into it.

landmarks.name: The Colosseum
landmarks.description: The iconic amphitheater of ancient Rome where gladiators fought and emperors entertained 50,000 spectators.

figures.name: Vespasian
figures.title: Roman Emperor, Builder of the Colosseum (9–79 AD)
figures.previewQuote: I built this arena to give Rome back to its people.

figures.name: Spartacus
figures.title: Gladiator and Leader of the Great Slave Revolt (c. 111–71 BC)
figures.previewQuote: They called us slaves. We called ourselves free.

figures.name: Livia Drusilla
figures.title: Empress of Rome, Wife of Augustus (58 BC–29 AD)
figures.previewQuote: Behind every emperor, there is someone who actually gets things done.

landmarks.name: The Acropolis
landmarks.description: The hilltop citadel of Athens crowned by the Parthenon, birthplace of democracy and Western philosophy.

figures.name: Pericles
figures.title: Statesman and General of Athens (495–429 BC)
figures.previewQuote: We do not imitate others — we are an example to them.

figures.name: Socrates
figures.title: Philosopher of Athens (470–399 BC)
figures.previewQuote: I know that I know nothing — and that makes me the wisest person in Athens!

figures.name: Aspasia
figures.title: Intellectual and Companion of Pericles (c. 470–400 BC)
figures.previewQuote: They say women cannot teach. Strange — Socrates himself came to learn from me.

landmarks.name: Stonehenge
landmarks.description: The mysterious circle of standing stones on Salisbury Plain, built over a thousand years by ancient peoples.

figures.name: Aelra (fictional)
figures.title: Master Stone Builder of Stonehenge (c. 2500 BC)
figures.previewQuote: We moved mountains — not for ourselves, but for the sky.

figures.name: Brighid (fictional)
figures.title: Keeper of the Sky Calendar (c. 2500 BC)
figures.previewQuote: The stones remember what the sky tells them.

figures.name: Boudica
figures.title: Queen of the Iceni (d. 60/61 AD)
figures.previewQuote: This land is ours. Every stone, every hill, every river.

landmarks.name: Tower of London
landmarks.description: The ancient fortress on the Thames that served as a royal palace, prison, and home of the Crown Jewels.

figures.name: William the Conqueror
figures.title: King of England (1028–1087)
figures.previewQuote: I crossed the sea, won a kingdom, and built this tower to keep it.

figures.name: Anne Boleyn
figures.title: Queen of England (c. 1501–1536)
figures.previewQuote: I was a queen who changed the world — and they locked me in my own castle.

figures.name: Guy Fawkes
figures.title: Conspirator of the Gunpowder Plot (1570–1606)
figures.previewQuote: Desperate times called for desperate measures — though I don't recommend mine.

landmarks.name: The Alhambra
landmarks.description: The stunning Moorish palace-fortress with intricate Islamic art, peaceful courtyards, and a rich multicultural history.

figures.name: Muhammad V
figures.title: Sultan of Granada (1338–1391)
figures.previewQuote: Every wall in my palace tells a story in stone and light.

figures.name: Fatima al-Fihri
figures.title: Founder of the World's First University (c. 800–880)
figures.previewQuote: I built a house of learning that has never closed its doors.

figures.name: Washington Irving
figures.title: American Author and Explorer of the Alhambra (1783–1859)
figures.previewQuote: I slept in these halls and heard the ghosts of sultans whispering.

landmarks.name: Pompeii
landmarks.description: The Roman city frozen in time by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD, perfectly preserved under volcanic ash.

figures.name: Pliny the Elder
figures.title: Roman Naturalist and Admiral (23–79 AD)
figures.previewQuote: I sailed toward the eruption, not away from it. Science demanded it.

figures.name: Eumachia
figures.title: Businesswoman and Priestess of Pompeii (1st Century AD)
figures.previewQuote: I built the largest building on the forum. Not bad for a woman in Rome.

figures.name: Terentius Neo
figures.title: Baker and Citizen of Pompeii (1st Century AD)
figures.previewQuote: I baked bread for a living. Turns out, that bread lasted two thousand years.

landmarks.name: Hagia Sophia
landmarks.description: The architectural wonder that served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum — a bridge between civilizations for 1,500 years.

figures.name: Justinian I
figures.title: Byzantine Emperor (482–565 AD)
figures.previewQuote: When the dome was finished, I whispered: Solomon, I have surpassed thee.

figures.name: Theodora
figures.title: Byzantine Empress (c. 497–548 AD)
figures.previewQuote: They told me an actress could never be empress. I proved them all wrong.

figures.name: Isidore of Miletus
figures.title: Architect of the Hagia Sophia (6th Century AD)
figures.previewQuote: They said a dome this large would collapse. I said — let me show you the mathematics.

landmarks.name: The Moscow Kremlin
landmarks.description: The fortified heart of Moscow, home to tsars and rulers for over 500 years.

figures.name: Ivan III (Ivan the Great)
figures.title: Grand Prince of Moscow (1440–1505)
figures.previewQuote: I freed Russia from foreign rule and built these walls to keep it free.

figures.name: Catherine the Great
figures.title: Empress of Russia (1729–1796)
figures.previewQuote: I came to Russia as a foreign princess. I left it as the most powerful woman in the world.

figures.name: Andrei Rublev
figures.title: Master Icon Painter (c. 1360–1430)
figures.previewQuote: I painted not with my hands, but with my soul.

landmarks.name: Edinburgh Castle
landmarks.description: The ancient fortress perched on a volcanic rock, commanding the Scottish capital for over 900 years.

figures.name: Mary, Queen of Scots
figures.title: Queen of Scotland (1542–1587)
figures.previewQuote: I became queen when I was six days old. It only got more complicated from there.

figures.name: Robert the Bruce
figures.title: King of Scotland (1274–1329)
figures.previewQuote: I lost six battles in a row. Then I watched a spider, and everything changed.

figures.name: John Gray
figures.title: Edinburgh Night Watchman and Owner of Greyfriars Bobby (d. 1858)
figures.previewQuote: I was just a watchman. My wee dog made me famous.

landmarks.name: Pyramids of Giza
landmarks.description: The last surviving Wonder of the Ancient World — massive tombs built for the pharaohs 4,500 years ago.

figures.name: Pharaoh Khufu
figures.title: Builder of the Great Pyramid (c. 2589–2566 BC)
figures.previewQuote: My pyramid will stand until the stars themselves grow old.

figures.name: Cleopatra VII
figures.title: Last Pharaoh of Egypt (69–30 BC)
figures.previewQuote: I spoke nine languages. I didn't need beauty — I had my mind.

figures.name: Hemiunu
figures.title: Architect of the Great Pyramid (c. 2570 BC)
figures.previewQuote: Every block is within millimeters of perfection. That was my job.

landmarks.name: Valley of the Kings
landmarks.description: The hidden valley where Egypt's greatest pharaohs were buried in elaborately decorated underground tombs.

figures.name: Tutankhamun
figures.title: The Boy King of Egypt (c. 1341–1323 BC)
figures.previewQuote: I became pharaoh at nine. My golden mask made me immortal.

figures.name: Hatshepsut
figures.title: Female Pharaoh of Egypt (c. 1507–1458 BC)
figures.previewQuote: They tried to erase me from history. Here I am, still standing.

figures.name: Howard Carter
figures.title: Archaeologist Who Discovered Tutankhamun's Tomb (1874–1939)
figures.previewQuote: I searched for years. Then I saw wonderful things.

landmarks.name: Great Zimbabwe
landmarks.description: The massive stone city that was the heart of a powerful southern African kingdom and trading empire.

figures.name: Nyatsimba Mutota
figures.title: Founder of the Mutapa Empire (15th Century)
figures.previewQuote: From these stone walls, we built an empire that reached the sea.

figures.name: Amina (fictional)
figures.title: Swahili Coast Trader at Great Zimbabwe (14th Century)
figures.previewQuote: I've traded from Kilwa to Gujarat. The world is bigger than you think.

landmarks.name: Timbuktu
landmarks.description: The legendary city of gold and learning on the edge of the Sahara, home to one of the world's great universities.

figures.name: Mansa Musa
figures.title: Emperor of Mali, Richest Person in History (c. 1280–1337)
figures.previewQuote: I gave away so much gold in Egypt that I crashed their economy. Oops.

figures.name: Ahmed Baba
figures.title: Scholar of Timbuktu (1556–1627)
figures.previewQuote: They burned my library. But they could not burn what I carry in my mind.

figures.name: Aisha (fictional)
figures.title: Trans-Saharan Salt Trader (15th Century)
figures.previewQuote: Twenty days across the hottest desert on Earth. That's just my Tuesday.

landmarks.name: Rock-Hewn Churches of Lalibela
landmarks.description: Eleven medieval churches carved directly downward into solid rock — an engineering and spiritual marvel.

figures.name: King Gebre Mesqel Lalibela
figures.title: King of the Zagwe Dynasty (c. 1162–1221)
figures.previewQuote: When pilgrims could not go to Jerusalem, I brought Jerusalem to them.

figures.name: Tekle (fictional)
figures.title: Master Rock Carver of Lalibela (13th Century)
figures.previewQuote: Each strike of my chisel was a prayer.

figures.name: Queen of Sheba / Makeda (fictional)
figures.title: Legendary Queen of Ethiopia
figures.previewQuote: I traveled to the ends of the earth seeking wisdom. Was it worth it? Always.

landmarks.name: Carthage
landmarks.description: The ancient Phoenician city that rivaled Rome for control of the Mediterranean world.

figures.name: Hannibal Barca
figures.title: Carthaginian General (247–c. 183 BC)
figures.previewQuote: I crossed the Alps with elephants. They said it was impossible. I said watch me.

figures.name: Queen Dido / Elissa (fictional)
figures.title: Legendary Founder of Carthage (c. 9th Century BC)
figures.previewQuote: They gave me only as much land as an ox hide could cover. So I cut it into strips.

figures.name: Hanno the Navigator
figures.title: Carthaginian Explorer (c. 500 BC)
figures.previewQuote: I sailed past the edge of the known world. What I found there was extraordinary.

landmarks.name: Robben Island
landmarks.description: The island prison where Nelson Mandela spent 18 years, now a powerful symbol of the triumph of the human spirit.

figures.name: Nelson Mandela
figures.title: Anti-Apartheid Leader and President of South Africa (1918–2013)
figures.previewQuote: I walked out of this prison after 27 years without hatred in my heart.

figures.name: Walter Sisulu
figures.title: Anti-Apartheid Leader and Political Mentor (1912–2003)
figures.previewQuote: I was the gardener who helped great trees grow.

figures.name: Ahmed Kathrada
figures.title: Anti-Apartheid Activist and Robben Island Prisoner (1929–2017)
figures.previewQuote: We turned a prison into a university. That was our rebellion.

landmarks.name: Elmina Castle
landmarks.description: The oldest European building in sub-Saharan Africa, a site central to understanding the transatlantic slave trade.

figures.name: Kwame (fictional)
figures.title: Local Historian and Descendant of Elmina (Present Day)
figures.previewQuote: We remember, so that it never happens again.

figures.name: Yaa Asantewaa
figures.title: Queen Mother of the Ashanti Empire (c. 1840–1921)
figures.previewQuote: If the men will not fight, then the women will.

figures.name: Nana Esi (fictional)
figures.title: Fante Fisherwoman and Elder of Elmina (18th Century)
figures.previewQuote: This was our home long before the ships came. It will be our home long after.

landmarks.name: Petra
landmarks.description: The 'Rose City' carved into pink sandstone cliffs by the Nabataean people — a crossroads of the ancient world.

figures.name: Aretas IV
figures.title: King of the Nabataeans (c. 9 BC–40 AD)
figures.previewQuote: We turned the desert into a garden and carved a city from the cliffs.

figures.name: Shaqilat (fictional)
figures.title: Nabataean Water Engineer (1st Century AD)
figures.previewQuote: In the desert, water is more precious than gold. I commanded both.

figures.name: Obodas (fictional)
figures.title: Nabataean Incense Trader (1st Century BC)
figures.previewQuote: Frankincense and myrrh made us richer than kings. Well, some of us WERE kings.

landmarks.name: Old City of Jerusalem
landmarks.description: One of the oldest and most sacred cities in the world, holy to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

figures.name: King Solomon
figures.title: King of Israel, Builder of the First Temple (c. 970–931 BC)
figures.previewQuote: They came from across the world to test my wisdom. Most left satisfied.

figures.name: Saladin
figures.title: Sultan of Egypt and Syria (1137–1193)
figures.previewQuote: I conquered Jerusalem — and then I protected its people, all of them.

figures.name: Helena
figures.title: Roman Empress and Christian Pilgrim (c. 248–330 AD)
figures.previewQuote: I was an empress who became a pilgrim. I came to Jerusalem to find the truth.

landmarks.name: Persepolis
landmarks.description: The ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Persian Empire — one of the largest empires the world has ever seen.

figures.name: Cyrus the Great
figures.title: Founder of the Achaemenid Empire (c. 600–530 BC)
figures.previewQuote: I conquered the world and let every people keep their gods, their languages, their ways.

figures.name: Darius the Great
figures.title: Persian Emperor and Builder of Persepolis (550–486 BC)
figures.previewQuote: I built roads that connected an empire and a palace that awed the world.

figures.name: Artemisia I
figures.title: Queen of Halicarnassus and Persian Naval Commander (5th Century BC)
figures.previewQuote: I was the only commander who gave the King of Persia advice he didn't want to hear.

landmarks.name: Taj Mahal
landmarks.description: The breathtaking white marble mausoleum built by a Mughal emperor as a monument to eternal love.

figures.name: Shah Jahan
figures.title: Mughal Emperor, Builder of the Taj Mahal (1592–1666)
figures.previewQuote: I built the Taj Mahal so the world would never forget what love looks like.

figures.name: Mumtaz Mahal
figures.title: Mughal Empress (1593–1631)
figures.previewQuote: He built the world's most beautiful building for me. But I would trade it all for one more day together.

figures.name: Ustad Ahmad Lahori
figures.title: Chief Architect of the Taj Mahal (17th Century)
figures.previewQuote: Perfect symmetry is not found in nature. But I built it in stone.

landmarks.name: Sigiriya
landmarks.description: The ancient fortress built atop a 200-meter rock column — one of the most dramatic sites in Asia.

figures.name: King Kashyapa I
figures.title: King of Sri Lanka (477–495 AD)
figures.previewQuote: I built my palace in the sky because I trusted no one on the ground.

figures.name: Devini (fictional)
figures.title: Court Painter of Sigiriya (5th Century AD)
figures.previewQuote: I painted masterpieces on the side of a cliff. My hands shook, but my brush did not.

figures.name: Ananda (fictional)
figures.title: Royal Garden Engineer of Sigiriya (5th Century AD)
figures.previewQuote: Carrying water to the top of a rock? Simple — if you understand pressure.

landmarks.name: Great Wall of China
landmarks.description: The longest structure ever built by humans, stretching over 20,000 kilometers across mountains and deserts.

figures.name: Qin Shi Huang
figures.title: First Emperor of China (259–210 BC)
figures.previewQuote: I unified China, built the Wall, and standardized everything from money to the width of roads.

figures.name: Hua Mulan (fictional)
figures.title: Legendary Warrior of China
figures.previewQuote: My father was too old to fight. So I took his place — and no one noticed for twelve years.

figures.name: Wei (fictional)
figures.title: Worker on the Great Wall (3rd Century BC)
figures.previewQuote: I haven't seen my family in three years. But the Wall grows longer every day.

landmarks.name: The Forbidden City
landmarks.description: The imperial palace complex that was home to 24 Chinese emperors — the largest palace in the world.

figures.name: The Yongle Emperor
figures.title: Emperor of the Ming Dynasty (1360–1424)
figures.previewQuote: I built this palace and sent ships to the ends of the earth.

figures.name: Empress Dowager Cixi
figures.title: Ruler of the Qing Dynasty (1835–1908)
figures.previewQuote: They said a woman could not rule China. I ruled it for 47 years.

figures.name: Zheng He
figures.title: Admiral and Explorer (1371–1433)
figures.previewQuote: My ships were five times larger than Columbus's. We reached Africa decades before Europe did.

landmarks.name: Terracotta Army
landmarks.description: An army of 8,000 life-sized clay soldiers buried to guard China's first emperor in the afterlife.

figures.name: Master Zhang (fictional)
figures.title: Chief Sculptor of the Terracotta Army (3rd Century BC)
figures.previewQuote: Eight thousand faces, and no two are the same. That was my life's work.

figures.name: Yang Zhifa
figures.title: Farmer Who Discovered the Terracotta Army (b. 1938)
figures.previewQuote: I was digging a well. I found the biggest archaeological treasure in history.

figures.name: General Meng Tian
figures.title: Qin Dynasty General (d. 210 BC)
figures.previewQuote: I defended the empire and built the Wall. My reward? Ask the Emperor.

landmarks.name: Angkor Wat
landmarks.description: The largest religious monument in the world, a masterpiece of Khmer architecture surrounded by jungle.

figures.name: Suryavarman II
figures.title: King of the Khmer Empire, Builder of Angkor Wat (c. 1090–1150)
figures.previewQuote: I built a temple so large it could hold the universe.

figures.name: Srey (fictional)
figures.title: Master Stone Carver of Angkor Wat (12th Century)
figures.previewQuote: Every figure I carve into stone is a story that will outlive us all.

figures.name: Jayavarman VII
figures.title: King of the Khmer Empire (c. 1122–1218)
figures.previewQuote: I built 102 hospitals across my kingdom. A king should heal, not just conquer.

landmarks.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
landmarks.description: The shimmering golden temple reflected in its mirror pond — a jewel of Japanese art and Zen Buddhism.

figures.name: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu
figures.title: Shogun of Japan (1358–1408)
figures.previewQuote: I covered my retirement villa in gold. Why? Because I could.

figures.name: Murasaki Shikibu
figures.title: Author of The Tale of Genji (c. 973–1014)
figures.previewQuote: I wrote the world's first novel. Everyone said it was just a woman's diary.

figures.name: Master Musō Soseki
figures.title: Zen Buddhist Monk and Garden Designer (1275–1351)
figures.previewQuote: A garden is not decoration. It is a path to understanding.

landmarks.name: Borobudur
landmarks.description: The world's largest Buddhist temple — a massive stone mandala built as a path to enlightenment.

figures.name: King Samaratungga
figures.title: Sailendra Dynasty King, Patron of Borobudur (9th Century)
figures.previewQuote: I built a mountain of stone to help people climb toward wisdom.

figures.name: Wira (fictional)
figures.title: Relief Sculptor of Borobudur (9th Century)
figures.previewQuote: Two thousand six hundred panels. Each one a page in the world's largest stone book.

figures.name: Sir Thomas Stamford Raffles
figures.title: British Governor who Rediscovered Borobudur (1781–1826)
figures.previewQuote: The jungle had swallowed an entire temple. I could barely believe my eyes.

landmarks.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
landmarks.description: The grand palace of the Joseon Dynasty, the largest of Seoul's five royal palaces.

figures.name: King Sejong the Great
figures.title: King of Joseon, Inventor of Hangul (1397–1450)
figures.previewQuote: I created a writing system so simple that anyone could learn it in a day.

figures.name: Jang Yeong-sil
figures.title: Inventor and Scientist of the Joseon Dynasty (15th Century)
figures.previewQuote: I was born a slave. I became the greatest inventor in Korea.

figures.name: Shin Saimdang
figures.title: Artist, Poet, and Scholar (1504–1551)
figures.previewQuote: I painted insects and flowers. My son grew up to be a great scholar. I'm proud of both.

landmarks.name: Himeji Castle
landmarks.description: The stunning 'White Heron Castle' — Japan's best-preserved feudal castle and a masterpiece of defensive design.

figures.name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
figures.title: Unifier of Japan (1537–1598)
figures.previewQuote: I started as a sandal-bearer. I ended up ruling Japan.

figures.name: Miyamoto Musashi
figures.title: Legendary Swordsman and Author (c. 1584–1645)
figures.previewQuote: I won 60 duels. Then I put down my sword and picked up a paintbrush.

figures.name: Senhime (Lady Sen)
figures.title: Princess and Resident of Himeji Castle (1597–1666)
figures.previewQuote: I survived wars, sieges, and heartbreak. This castle was my sanctuary.

landmarks.name: Uluru (Ayers Rock)
landmarks.description: The sacred sandstone monolith at the heart of Australia, central to the world's oldest continuous culture.

figures.name: Tjilpi / Elder (fictional)
figures.title: Anangu Elder and Keeper of Tjukurpa (Present Day)
figures.previewQuote: This rock has stories older than your pyramids, older than your cities.

figures.name: Kunmanara (fictional)
figures.title: Anangu Tracker and Desert Survivor (Present Day)
figures.previewQuote: The desert looks empty to you. To me, it's full of food, water, and stories.

figures.name: Yalti (fictional)
figures.title: Anangu Artist and Painter (Present Day)
figures.previewQuote: When I paint, I'm painting the land's stories — not just pictures.

landmarks.name: Waitangi Treaty Grounds
landmarks.description: The place where the founding document of New Zealand was signed between the British Crown and Māori chiefs.

figures.name: Hone Heke
figures.title: Māori Rangatira (Chief) (c. 1807–1850)
figures.previewQuote: I was the first to sign the Treaty. I was also the first to fight for what it truly promised.

figures.name: Meri Te Tai Mangakāhia
figures.title: Māori Women's Rights Pioneer (1868–1920)
figures.previewQuote: I stood before the Māori Parliament and demanded that women have the right to vote.

figures.name: Kupe (fictional)
figures.title: Legendary Polynesian Navigator
figures.previewQuote: I navigated by the stars across the largest ocean on Earth.

landmarks.name: Chichén Itzá
landmarks.description: The magnificent Maya city dominated by the pyramid of Kukulcán, where a feathered serpent shadow descends each equinox.

figures.name: Ah Kin (fictional)
figures.title: High Priest and Astronomer of Chichén Itzá (10th Century)
figures.previewQuote: Twice a year, the feathered serpent descends the pyramid. We designed it that way.

figures.name: Lady Xoc
figures.title: Maya Noble and Scholar (8th Century)
figures.previewQuote: While Europe was in its Dark Ages, we were writing books and mapping the stars.

figures.name: Hunahpu (fictional)
figures.title: Champion Ball Player of Chichén Itzá (10th Century)
figures.previewQuote: Our ball game was like your football, basketball, and a religious ceremony all at once.

landmarks.name: Teotihuacán
landmarks.description: The massive ancient city of pyramids — once one of the largest cities in the world, built by a mysterious civilization.

figures.name: Citlali (fictional)
figures.title: Architect of the Pyramid of the Sun (2nd Century AD)
figures.previewQuote: We built a city for 100,000 people with pyramids taller than anything in the Americas.

figures.name: Xochitl (fictional)
figures.title: Mural Painter of Teotihuacán (5th Century AD)
figures.previewQuote: Our walls exploded with color — jaguars, birds, and gods in red and green and gold.

figures.name: Obsidian Merchant (fictional)
figures.title: Obsidian Trader of Teotihuacán (3rd Century AD)
figures.previewQuote: Obsidian was our steel, our currency, our most precious resource.

landmarks.name: Mesa Verde
landmarks.description: The breathtaking cliff dwellings built into canyon walls by the Ancestral Puebloan people.

figures.name: Kwiiyagat (fictional)
figures.title: Master Builder of the Cliff Dwellings (13th Century)
figures.previewQuote: We built our homes inside the cliffs — protected from snow, rain, and enemies.

figures.name: Tse'pinah (fictional)
figures.title: Potter and Artist of Mesa Verde (12th Century)
figures.previewQuote: Every pot I make tells the story of my people and our connection to the earth.

figures.name: Sun Watcher (fictional)
figures.title: Calendar Keeper of Mesa Verde (13th Century)
figures.previewQuote: I watch where the sun rises each day. When it reaches the right spot, it's time to plant.

landmarks.name: Independence Hall
landmarks.description: The birthplace of the United States, where the Declaration of Independence and Constitution were debated and signed.

figures.name: Benjamin Franklin
figures.title: Founding Father, Inventor, and Diplomat (1706–1790)
figures.previewQuote: I invented bifocals, discovered electricity, and helped start a country. Not bad for a printer.

figures.name: Abigail Adams
figures.title: First Lady and Political Advisor (1744–1818)
figures.previewQuote: I told them to remember the ladies. They didn't listen. Yet.

figures.name: James Forten
figures.title: African American Sail Maker and Abolitionist (1766–1842)
figures.previewQuote: I fought for this country's freedom at age 14. Then I spent my life fighting for mine.

landmarks.name: Machu Picchu
landmarks.description: The Inca citadel hidden high in the Andes mountains, one of the most spectacular archaeological sites in the world.

figures.name: Pachacuti
figures.title: Inca Emperor, Builder of Machu Picchu (1418–1471)
figures.previewQuote: I transformed a small kingdom into the largest empire in the Americas.

figures.name: Quilla (fictional)
figures.title: Inca Engineer and Quipu Keeper (15th Century)
figures.previewQuote: We had no writing. Instead, we kept records with knotted strings — and they worked perfectly.

figures.name: Hiram Bingham III
figures.title: Explorer Who Brought Machu Picchu to World Attention (1875–1956)
figures.previewQuote: A local farmer led me up a mountain. What I found changed archaeology forever.

landmarks.name: Rapa Nui (Easter Island)
landmarks.description: The remote Pacific island famous for its massive stone head statues (moai), carved by Polynesian settlers.

figures.name: Ariki Tupa (fictional)
figures.title: Master Moai Carver of Rapa Nui (15th Century)
figures.previewQuote: Each statue carries the spirit of an ancestor. That's why they face inland — watching over us.

figures.name: Tu'u Ko Iho (fictional)
figures.title: Polynesian Navigator Who Settled Rapa Nui (c. 10th Century)
figures.previewQuote: We sailed to the most remote island on Earth. On purpose.

figures.name: Tangata Manu (fictional)
figures.title: Birdman Competition Champion (17th Century)
figures.previewQuote: I climbed down a cliff, swam through shark water, and brought back an egg. That made me king for a year.

landmarks.name: Tikal
landmarks.description: The towering Maya city rising above the jungle canopy — once home to 100,000 people.

figures.name: Jasaw Chan K'awiil I
figures.title: King of Tikal (c. 682–734 AD)
figures.previewQuote: I brought Tikal back from defeat and built the tallest pyramid in the Maya world.

figures.name: Ixchel (fictional)
figures.title: Royal Chocolate Maker of Tikal (7th Century)
figures.previewQuote: Chocolate wasn't candy — it was a sacred drink, and I made it for kings.

figures.name: Ahau Kin (fictional)
figures.title: Maya Astronomer of Tikal (8th Century)
figures.previewQuote: We predicted eclipses centuries into the future. With no telescopes. Just patience.

landmarks.name: Gettysburg Battlefield
landmarks.description: The site of the Civil War's turning-point battle and Lincoln's famous address about democracy and equality.

figures.name: Abraham Lincoln
figures.title: 16th President of the United States (1809–1865)
figures.previewQuote: In just 272 words, I tried to explain what all those soldiers died for.

figures.name: Harriet Tubman
figures.title: Abolitionist, Scout, and Liberator (c. 1822–1913)
figures.previewQuote: I freed myself, then went back for everyone else. Thirteen trips, and I never lost a passenger.

figures.name: Joshua Lawrence Chamberlain
figures.title: Union Colonel and Hero of Little Round Top (1828–1914)
figures.previewQuote: We were out of ammunition. So I ordered a bayonet charge. Downhill. It worked.

landmarks.name: Registan Square, Samarkand
landmarks.description: The dazzling heart of the Silk Road — a square framed by three magnificent madrasas covered in turquoise tile.

figures.name: Timur (Tamerlane)
figures.title: Conqueror and Founder of the Timurid Empire (1336–1405)
figures.previewQuote: I conquered half the known world, then filled my capital with artists and scholars.

figures.name: Ulugh Beg
figures.title: Astronomer-King of Samarkand (1394–1449)
figures.previewQuote: My grandfather conquered with swords. I conquered with telescopes.

figures.name: Sogdian Merchant (fictional)
figures.title: Silk Road Trader of Samarkand (7th Century)
figures.previewQuote: I speak six languages because money speaks all of them.

landmarks.name: Palace of Knossos
landmarks.description: The legendary palace of the Minoans — Europe's first great civilization, with its myth of the Minotaur's labyrinth.

figures.name: King Minos (fictional)
figures.title: Legendary King of Crete
figures.previewQuote: They say I kept a monster in a maze. The truth is more interesting than the myth.

figures.name: Ariadne (fictional)
figures.title: Minoan High Priestess (c. 1600 BC)
figures.previewQuote: In Crete, women held the sacred power. Remember that.

figures.name: Icarus (fictional)
figures.title: Bull Leaper of Knossos (c. 1500 BC)
figures.previewQuote: You think your sports are exciting? I jump over charging bulls.

landmarks.name: Viking Ship Museum
landmarks.description: Home to the best-preserved Viking ships in the world — vessels that sailed from Scandinavia to North America.

figures.name: Leif Erikson
figures.title: Viking Explorer Who Reached North America (c. 970–1020)
figures.previewQuote: I reached America 500 years before Columbus. In a Viking ship. Without a map.

figures.name: Queen Asa
figures.title: Viking Queen of the Oseberg Ship (9th Century)
figures.previewQuote: They buried me in the most beautiful ship ever built. I must have been very important indeed.

figures.name: Thorvald (fictional)
figures.title: Viking Master Shipbuilder (10th Century)
figures.previewQuote: My ships could cross oceans and sail up rivers. Try that with your modern boats.

landmarks.name: Mohenjo-daro
landmarks.description: One of the world's first great cities, built by the mysterious Indus Valley Civilization with advanced urban planning.

figures.name: The City Planner (fictional)
figures.title: Urban Planner of Mohenjo-daro (c. 2400 BC)
figures.previewQuote: We had indoor plumbing four thousand years ago. You're welcome.

figures.name: Priya (fictional)
figures.title: Bead Maker and Artisan of Mohenjo-daro (c. 2300 BC)
figures.previewQuote: My tiny beads traveled to Mesopotamia. The whole ancient world wore my jewelry.

figures.name: The Seal Maker (fictional)
figures.title: Seal Carver and Record Keeper (c. 2400 BC)
figures.previewQuote: I carve seals with writing nobody today can read. The secret dies with my civilization.

landmarks.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
landmarks.description: The largest mud-brick building in the world — rebuilt annually by the entire community in an extraordinary tradition.

figures.name: Barey Ton (fictional)
figures.title: Master Mason of the Djenné Building Guild (Present Day)
figures.previewQuote: Every year, the whole city comes together to repair our mosque. It's the biggest party in Mali.

figures.name: Alfa Sidy (fictional)
figures.title: Scholar of the Djenné Manuscripts (16th Century)
figures.previewQuote: Djenné held more knowledge than most European cities ever dreamed of.

figures.name: Aminata (fictional)
figures.title: Market Trader of Djenné (Present Day)
figures.previewQuote: Monday is market day. Ten thousand people come from everywhere. Welcome to my world!

landmarks.name: Templo Mayor (Tenochtitlán)
landmarks.description: The great temple at the heart of the Aztec capital, a city built on a lake that amazed Spanish conquistadors.

figures.name: Moctezuma II
figures.title: Aztec Emperor (c. 1466–1520)
figures.previewQuote: My city on the lake had 200,000 people. The Spanish had never seen anything like it.

figures.name: Tlanextli (fictional)
figures.title: Chinampa Farmer of Tenochtitlán (15th Century)
figures.previewQuote: We grow our food on floating gardens. Yes, floating. On the lake.

figures.name: Malintzin (La Malinche)
figures.title: Interpreter and Key Figure of the Spanish-Aztec Encounter (c. 1500–1529)
figures.previewQuote: I spoke the languages that changed the course of history. Judge me as you will.

landmarks.name: Tiwanaku
landmarks.description: The ancient capital of a powerful Andean civilization at 3,850 meters above sea level, near Lake Titicaca.

figures.name: Khuno (fictional)
figures.title: Master Architect of Tiwanaku (8th Century)
figures.previewQuote: We built a city at the top of the world. The air is thin, but our ambitions were not.

figures.name: Sisa (fictional)
figures.title: Agricultural Engineer of the Raised Fields (9th Century)
figures.previewQuote: Everyone said you can't farm this high up. We proved them spectacularly wrong.

figures.name: Thunupa (fictional)
figures.title: Priest of the Gateway of the Sun (9th Century)
figures.previewQuote: The Gateway of the Sun marks the turning of the seasons. It is where time begins.

landmarks.name: Nazca Lines
landmarks.description: Giant drawings in the desert — hummingbirds, monkeys, and spiders visible only from the sky — made 2,000 years ago.

figures.name: Tupaq (fictional)
figures.title: Master Line Maker of the Nazca (3rd Century AD)
figures.previewQuote: We made drawings so large they can only be seen from the sky. The gods can see them.

figures.name: Qori (fictional)
figures.title: Water Engineer of the Nazca Aqueducts (5th Century AD)
figures.previewQuote: The lines get all the fame. But our underground aqueducts? Those kept us alive.

figures.name: Chaska (fictional)
figures.title: Master Textile Weaver of Nazca (4th Century AD)
figures.previewQuote: Our textiles had more colors than a rainbow and told stories that lasted centuries.

landmarks.name: Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani
landmarks.description: The ruins of the wealthiest Swahili trading city on the East African coast, controlling gold and ivory routes.

figures.name: Sultan Ali ibn al-Hasan
figures.title: Founder of the Kilwa Sultanate (10th–11th Century)
figures.previewQuote: From this small island, I built a trade empire that stretched across the ocean.

figures.name: Fatima bint Khalid (fictional)
figures.title: Master Coin Maker of Kilwa (13th Century)
figures.previewQuote: We minted our own coins. That's how the world knew Kilwa was a real power.

figures.name: Ibn Battuta's Host (fictional)
figures.title: Kilwa Merchant and Host to the World's Greatest Traveler (14th Century)
figures.previewQuote: The greatest traveler in the world called Kilwa the most beautiful city he'd seen.
